_about: Hand-authored mapping from FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators to the AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, with 2022 points of focus). Criteria are identified by number; the criteria text belongs to the AICPA and is not reproduced. 'strong' means a SOC 2 report with that criterion in scope and no exception substantially evidences the indicator's outcome; 'partial' covers part of it. 'adds' is what 20x asks for beyond what a clean SOC 2 shows. Version 1, open to review.

KSI-CED-RAT.adds: SOC 2 shows training happens and competence is maintained. 20x wants training split by audience (general, high-risk roles, engineers on secure delivery, incident and recovery staff) and its effectiveness reviewed on a cadence.

KSI-CMT-LMC.adds: SOC 2 tests a sample of change tickets. 20x wants every modification to the service logged and monitored at the resource level, continuously.

KSI-CMT-RMV.adds: Resources are redeployed from a known-good definition rather than modified in place. SOC 2 is indifferent to how a change is applied.

KSI-CMT-RVP.adds: Change procedures are reviewed persistently with evidence, including the automation that applies them.

KSI-CMT-VTD.adds: Validation runs throughout deployment for each change: automated tests, staged rollout, and checks after release, with artifacts kept.

KSI-CNA-DFP.adds: Functionality and privileges are defined per resource and kept to the minimum the service needs, in cloud-native terms.

KSI-CNA-EIS.adds: Automation assesses every machine-based resource and enforces its intended state, correcting drift. SOC 2 accepts periodic configuration review.

KSI-CNA-IBP.adds: The cloud platform's own best practices (its well-architected guidance) are followed and the evidence is kept current.

KSI-CNA-MAT.adds: Attack surface is minimized and measured continuously: exposed ports, services, endpoints and identities, including egress.

KSI-CNA-OFA.adds: Availability is engineered cloud-natively: multiple zones, scaling, and denial-of-service protection for the federal boundary. Needs the Availability category in scope.

KSI-CNA-RNT.adds: Traffic between all resources is denied by default and the policy is monitored persistently, not reviewed periodically.

KSI-CNA-RVP.adds: Boundary and denial-of-service protections are reviewed persistently against current threats, with evidence.

KSI-CNA-ULN.adds: Segmentation is logical (virtual networks, micro-segmentation) across every component of the service.

KSI-IAM-AAM.adds: The account lifecycle (join, move, leave) is automated and reviewed persistently. SOC 2 accepts ticket-driven provisioning with quarterly reviews.

KSI-IAM-APM.adds: Phishing-resistant MFA or passwordless methods for all users, aligned to NIST SP 800-63. SOC 2 does not specify authenticator strength.

KSI-IAM-ELP.adds: Least privilege is demonstrated with evidence and reviewed persistently, for machine identities as well as people.

KSI-IAM-JIT.adds: Authorization is just-in-time and attribute-based for every account and service. SOC 2 permits standing privileged access.

KSI-IAM-SNU.adds: Non-user identities (services, workloads, automation) authenticate with rotated credentials or mutual TLS and never with shared secrets.

KSI-IAM-SUS.adds: Suspicious account activity is detected and responded to automatically: lockout, session revocation, alerting.

KSI-INR-AAR.adds: An after-action report follows every incident and is shared with FedRAMP and affected agencies under the incident rules.

KSI-INR-RIR.adds: Procedures are reviewed against FedRAMP's incident communication rules: US-CERT reporting and agency notification timelines.

KSI-INR-RPI.adds: Past incidents are reviewed on a cadence for patterns, with documented improvements.

KSI-MLA-ALA.adds: Access to log data is just-in-time and attribute-based according to the data's sensitivity.

KSI-MLA-EVC.adds: Configurations are evaluated continuously and automatically against benchmarks (cloud security posture management).

KSI-MLA-LET.adds: The event types to log are defined for the federal boundary (administrative actions, authentication, data access) and applied to every resource.

KSI-MLA-OSM.adds: A SIEM-like capability correlates logs centrally, alerts, and retains them for the period FedRAMP expects.

KSI-MLA-RVL.adds: Logs, including privileged actions, are reviewed on a documented cadence with evidence of each review.

KSI-PIY-GIV.adds: A machine-generated, continuously accurate inventory of all information resources. SOC 2 rarely tests an inventory directly.

KSI-PIY-RES.adds: Executive support for security is reviewed persistently. Board oversight tested under CC1 is close, if it is evidenced.

KSI-PIY-RIS.adds: Investment in security is reviewed with budget and staffing evidence, not only governance minutes.

KSI-PIY-RSD.adds: Security in the development lifecycle is reviewed persistently and extends to software supply chain evidence such as SBOMs.

KSI-PIY-RVD.adds: A public vulnerability disclosure program with a published policy and intake. SOC 2 has no equivalent criterion.

KSI-RPL-ABO.adds: Backups are aligned to stated recovery objectives, tested, and protected from tampering. Needs the Availability category in scope.

KSI-RPL-ARP.adds: The recovery plan is specific to the federal service and aligned to its objectives, and is reported under FedRAMP's rules.

KSI-RPL-RRO.adds: Recovery time and point objectives are defined for the service and reviewed persistently.

KSI-RPL-TRC.adds: Recovery is exercised on a defined cadence with recorded results. Needs the Availability category in scope.

KSI-SCR-MIT.adds: FedRAMP-certified services are used where available, and every third-party resource is declared in the package overview.

KSI-SCR-MON.adds: Suppliers are monitored persistently, including vulnerability feeds for the components they provide.

KSI-SVC-ACM.adds: Configuration is managed as code and applied by automation, with the definitions as the evidence.

KSI-SVC-ASM.adds: Secrets are vaulted, rotated and injected automatically; none live in code or configuration files.

KSI-SVC-EIS.adds: Evaluation is persistent (automated scanning, penetration testing) and remediation follows FedRAMP's vulnerability timelines.

KSI-SVC-PRR.adds: After each change, plans and resources are reviewed for residual elements such as orphaned resources and stale configuration.

KSI-SVC-RUD.adds: Federal customer data is removed promptly on an agency's request, including from backups, with spill handling defined. Needs the Confidentiality category in scope.

KSI-SVC-SIN.adds: Cryptography is FIPS 140-validated for data at rest and in transit. SOC 2 does not name a validation program.

KSI-SVC-VCM.adds: Communications between machine resources are mutually authenticated and integrity-checked by automation (mutual TLS, signed messages).

KSI-SVC-VRI.adds: Resource integrity is validated with signed images, attestations and software bills of materials.
